title: I built a game with AI, then used AI to overhaul its visuals.
author: Dependent-Video7534
selftext:
Hi everyone! Back in April, I used Claude to help develop a zombie tower defense game and released it on Steam.

I was using Opus 4.7 at the time. Many of the visual effects were fairly basic, and the character animations had very few frames, so the overall presentation looked a bit rough.

Recently, I revisited the game with Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 to improve its visuals. I’ve been pleasantly surprised by how much AI-assisted development has progressed. With their help, I’ve been able to improve the character animations, pixel-style effects, and UI design.

There’s still room for improvement, but I’m much happier with how the game looks now compared to the original version.

  
Old  version：https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ADej31QogVU  


If you’re curious, there’s a free demo on Steam. I’d love to hear what you think of the updated visuals.

STEAM PAGE：https://store.steampowered.com/app/4609110/BULLET\_GIRLZOMBIE\_DEFENSE/?beta=0

comments.author: simon_is_high
comments.body: Darf ich fragen wie dein Workflow war um so konsistente Animationen zu bekommen?

replies.author: Dependent-Video7534
replies.body: I use GPT and Gemini’s image generation tools to create the characters and some action poses, then use Ludo to turn them into animations.

replies.author: simon_is_high
replies.body: Oooh thank you so much! Never heard of Ludo but thats exactly what Im looking for

comments.author: Jolly-Rip5973
comments.body: This could actually work if you had more stages and a story line.

replies.author: Dependent-Video7534
replies.body: Thanks for the valuable feedback! I’m planning to add more stages and new game modes featuring elite enemies, but everything is still in the planning phase.

comments.author: Any_Inevitable_4035
comments.body: Even those insecure AI haters can't differentiate.

replies.author: Dependent-Video7534
replies.body: Thank you so much! I think AI is a great tool for helping people bring their dreams to life. When used thoughtfully, it can help us create some really wonderful things.
